title: Give me the ball: verbs with two objects
tagline: Give, send, show, buy: say who gets the thing, in two different ways.
why: Verbs like give, send and buy have two objects: a person and a thing. You need both patterns to write messages and to speak naturally: Send me a text or Send it to me. The exam checks word order in short gaps.

hook.text: Miss Vega has a prize. "I'll give Nadia the book," she says. "Look, Nadia — I bought it for you!" Then Liam asks: "Can you show it to me?"
hook.ask: Which sentences have a person and a thing after the verb? Look at the small words to and for.

diagrams.title: Two ways to say the same thing
diagrams.caption: Person first: no to. Thing first: add to or for.

diagrams.title: How to choose the pattern

steps.label: Is the thing it or them?
Yes: put the thing first, then to or for
No: you can put the person first

diagrams.caption: With it or them, always use the to / for pattern.

head: Pattern
Example
Note
rows: She sent a message to me.
give, send, show, bring, lend, tell
He made a cake for her.
verb + it / them + to / for + person

examples.note: us = the people, homework = the thing

examples.text: I sent a message to my gran.

use.point: With it and them: thing first
Object pronouns: me, you, him, her, us, them

watch_out.wrong: She sent to me a message.
He bought to me a gift.

watch_out.why: After the verb use her, not she.
The person comes before the thing.

watch_out.wrong: I bought a bike to him.
watch_out.why: Buy and make go with for.

l1.why: Spanish puts two small words together. In English it goes before to + person.

l1.es: Le di el libro a Nadia.
l1.wrong: I gave to Nadia the book.
l1.why: The Spanish a becomes to only after the thing: I gave the book to Nadia.
No to when the person comes first.
With it, put the thing first and add to.

remember.trick: It or them? Thing first: give it to her.
remember.tip: Person first, no small word. Thing first, add to (give, send, show) or for (buy, make). With it and them, always thing first.

dialogue.title: Birthday prizes
dialogue.context: Miss Vega gives prizes to the students after the end-of-term quiz.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Well done, everyone. I've got something for you. First, I'll give Sofia a book.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Thank you, Miss! Can I show it to Nadia?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Yes, show it to me! I love new books.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: And Mateo, I bought a game for you.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Thanks! Liam, I'll lend it to you on Monday.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Great! Can you send me a message before?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Sure. I'll send you the time tonight.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good. Now pass me those papers, please.

can_do: I can say give me the ball and give the ball to me and I know both are right.
I can use to with give, send and show, and for with buy and make.
I can say Give it to her (not give her it) and use me, him, her, us and them.
summary: Two objects: person + thing (give me the ball) or thing + to/for + person (give the ball to me).
To goes with give, send, show, bring, lend, tell. For goes with buy, make, cook.
With it or them, put the thing first: give it to her.
After the verb use object pronouns: me, you, him, her, us, them.
